theorem_1_1_weight_exists: A smooth bump centered at \(1/2\) gives a nonzero, nonnegative, symmetric weight supported in \([1/3,2/3]\).
lemma_3_5_weight_support: For \(N>0\), if both weights are nonzero, the two nonzero difference families vanish; the sum family has only \(k=1\), so \(n+m=N\).
lemma_7_2_convolutions: Both convolutions are integrable; the half-line formulas equal the corresponding finite-interval integrals and recover the weight mass at \(y=1\).
proposition_7_4_norm_integrals: For \(N>0\) and every real boundary parameter, the energy and actual weight-norm integrals are integrable.
weightMass_pos: Strict positivity of the weight mass
The squared integral of a continuous nonzero weight is strictly positive, supplying the denominator in relative errors and prime-pair lower bounds.
weightMass_nonneg: The integral of the squared weight is nonnegative.
weightEnergy_nonneg: The squared derivative weight divided by the positive coordinate has a nonnegative half-line integral.
normFunctional_le_exp2_weightEnergy: Uniform upper bound for the weight norm
For \(N>e^{10}\), the integral formula and support yield \(Q_N\le e^2\,\mathrm{weightEnergy}(\phi)\).
badGoldbachMass: The original correlation range, coprimality condition, and two weights select terms where at least one entry is not prime.
badGoldbachMass_le_psi_sub_theta: Controlling higher-power terms by ψ − θ
The two-weight contribution is at most \((2\log N/N)(\psi(N)-\theta(N))\).
badGoldbachMass_le_sqrt: Explicit bound for higher prime powers
Mathlib Chebyshev estimates give the upper bound \(4(\log N)^2/\sqrt N\).
goldbach_le_badGoldbachMass_add_primePai: From weighted correlation to prime-pair counts
Split the finite sum into prime-pair and higher-power terms. Each prime pair contributes at most \((\log N)^2/N\).
companion_contDiff: The original weight vanishes near zero, so multiplying by the square root preserves global smoothness.
derivativeWeight_support_subset: The derivative weight remains supported in the closed support of the original weight.
